cohort: The study included women with persistent symptoms after perineal tears (N=170), primiparous women giving birth by caesarean section (N=54), and nulliparous women (N=338).
finding: The study developed and validated the 11-item Karolinska Symptoms After Perineal Tear Inventory, which is a psychometrically valid patient-reported outcome measure for symptoms of deficient perineum capable of distinguishing patients from controls with high sensitivity and specificity.
mod_finding: Women with confirmed deficient perineum after vaginal birth scored significantly higher on the symptoms inventory than primiparous women giving birth by caesarean section, indicating the inventory's ability to differentiate symptoms related to birth mode.
followup_time: more than one year after vaginal delivery/birth
cross-section timing: more than one year after vaginal delivery/birth
